title: A. Simple Permutation
statement:
Given an integer n. Construct a permutation p_1, p_2, …, p_n of length n that satisfies the following property:

For 1 ≤ i ≤ n, define c_i = lceil (p_1+p_2+… +p_i)/i rceil, then among c_1,c_2,…,c_n there must be at least lfloor n/3 rfloor - 1 prime numbers.

The first line contains an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10) — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows.

In a single line of each test case, there is a single integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) — the size of the permutation.

For each test case, output the permutation p_1,p_2,…,p_n of length n that satisfies the condition. It is guaranteed that such a permutation always exists.

In the first test case, c_1 = lceil 2/1 rceil = 2, c_2 = lceil (2+1)/2 rceil = 2. Both are prime numbers.

In the third test case, c_1 = lceil 2/1 rceil = 2, c_2 = lceil 3/2 rceil = 2, c_3 = lceil 6/3 rceil = 2, c_4 = lceil 10/4 rceil = 3, c_5 = lceil 15/5 rceil = 3. All these numbers are prime.

Input:
```
3235
```

Output:
```
2 1
2 1 3
2 1 3 4 5
```
